title: The Forgotten Choir
premise: Mirabel Yarrow has survived three years in the city of Vellamere by hiding her gift behind mundane cartography and harmless charms, but when the crown's witch-hunters begin dragging the gifted into the streets, she flees with a stolen map that reveals the Forgotten Choir—a buried sanctuary where the last free mages sleep in enchanted stasis. Pursued by Inquisitor Dain Corvane, who is himself a suppressed mage serving the throne, Mirabel must decide whether waking the Choir will save her people or reignite the war that nearly destroyed the world. Along the way she gathers a found family of hunted strays: a disgraced priest, a child prodigy, and an old smuggler who knew her mother. In the end, Mirabel wakes the Choir not as weapons but as witnesses, forcing Corvane to choose his own kind over his crown, and she inherits not her mother's war but her mother's unfinished map—one that leads somewhere no one has ever returned from.
about_author: Rosalind Galloway is the pen name of a former archivist who spent a decade cataloguing medieval maps before turning to fiction, and whose love of marginalia and half-erased place names infuses every page of her work. She writes fantasy about people who carry too much history in too small a body, and lives somewhere deliberately unmapped.

chapters.title: The Weight of Small Charms
chapters.summary: Mirabel's POV. In the market city of Vellamere, Mirabel sells luck-knots and weather charms disguised as folk craft while secretly mapping the unmapped realms that bleed through the city's edges. When royal criers announce a bounty on anyone with the gift, her neighbor—a hedge-witch who once sheltered her—is taken in broad daylight. The emotional beat is fear curdling into guilt: invisibility, Mirabel realizes, was always a luxury someone else paid for.

chapters.title: What the Map Remembers
chapters.summary: Mirabel's POV, with a brief interlude from Inquisitor Corvane. Fleeing the purge, Mirabel steals back her mother's confiscated atlas and discovers annotations pointing to the Forgotten Choir, a stasis-sleeping sanctuary of the last free mages. She gathers fellow fugitives—the defrocked priest Anselm, the mage-child Wren, and smuggler Old Bette. The beat is reluctant leadership: Mirabel stops running alone and starts carrying others.

chapters.title: The Hunt Beneath the Mountain
chapters.summary: Alternating POV between Mirabel and Corvane. The fugitives reach the mountain vault as Corvane's hunters close in; a betrayal by a frightened ally forces them into the flooded lower galleries, where Mirabel's cartography becomes survival itself. Corvane corners her at the Choir's threshold and confesses what he is. The climax: Mirabel wakes the sleeping mages—choosing revelation over safety—and the mountain answers with light.

chapters.title: A Chorus for the Unmapped
chapters.summary: Mirabel's POV. The awakened Choir refuses to fight, offering testimony instead, and their witness turns the city against the crown's lies; Corvane publicly breaks with his order and buys the fugitives time to scatter. Mirabel buries her mother's atlas and begins a new map—of the road beyond the known world—with Wren, Anselm, and Bette beside her. The resolution is bittersweet inheritance: survival was never free, but it can be shared.
